question: Which god is the ruler and supreme judge of the kingdom of the dead
explanation: Murdered by Seth and then brought back to life, Osiris rules the afterlife and judges the dead there.

question: Which god stands at the head of the Ennead of Heliopolis
explanation: The demiurge Atum, often merged with Re under the name Re-Atum, stands at the head of the nine gods of the Ennead.

question: What is the name of the primordial ocean from which everything emerged
explanation: Before Creation there was only the Nun, an inert, dark ocean that still surrounds the world.

question: Which giant serpent must the sun god face every night
explanation: Every night, the serpent Apophis attacks the bark of Re in the underworld to swallow the sun.

question: What is the name of the deified sun disc that Akhenaten made the only god of Egypt
explanation: The Aten is the sun disc itself, shown with rays ending in small hands.

question: What is the world of the dead called in Egyptian mythology
explanation: The Duat is the underworld that the sun crosses every night and through which the deceased travels.

question: What is the name of the primordial mound that rose from the Nun at Heliopolis
explanation: Atum raised a mound of earth out of the waters of the Nun, the Benben, so that he could stand on it.

question: Which god personifies air and light
explanation: Born of Atum’s sneeze, Shu is the god of air and light who holds up the sky.

question: Which goddess personifies moisture
explanation: Tefnut, born of Atum’s spittle, is the goddess of moisture, sister and wife of Shu.

question: Which god personifies the earth
explanation: Geb is the earth, shown lying beneath the arched body of Nut; earthquakes were said to be his laughter.

question: Which goddess personifies the sky
explanation: Nut is the sky: a woman with a star-covered body, arched above the earth.

question: Who is the wife of Osiris
explanation: Isis is the sister and wife of Osiris, whose dismembered body she gathered.

question: Who is the wife of Seth
explanation: Nephthys is the wife of Seth, but she took the side of Osiris after his murder.

question: How many children did Nut bring into the world during the epagomenal days
explanation: During the five epagomenal days, Osiris, Horus the Elder, Seth, Isis and Nephthys were born.

question: Which hieroglyph does the goddess Isis wear on her head
explanation: The name of Isis is written with the sign of the throne, which she wears on her head.

question: In what form does the sun god appear at daybreak
explanation: In the morning, the sun is Khepri, the scarab pushing the sun disc across the sky.

question: Under what name does the sun god reign at noon
explanation: The sun is Khepri in the morning, Re at noon in all his might, and Atum in the evening.

question: Under what name does the sun god set in the evening
explanation: In the evening, the sun becomes Atum, the old creator who sets in the west.

question: Which god embodies the desert, storms and disorder
explanation: Seth is the god of the desert, of storms and of disorder, associated with the colour red.

question: Which organ did the goddess Nephthys protect among the canopic jars
explanation: Nephthys watched over the canopic jar of the lungs, guarded by Hapy, the baboon-headed son of Horus.

question: Which god was born of the union of Osiris and Nephthys
explanation: According to the most widespread tradition, Anubis is the son of Osiris and Nephthys, raised by Isis.

question: Into how many pieces did Seth cut the body of Osiris
explanation: Seth cut the body of Osiris into fourteen pieces, which he scattered all over Egypt.

question: Which god was born of the union of Osiris and Isis
explanation: Isis conceived Horus by Osiris, revived by her magic, then hid him in the marshes of Chemmis.

question: Which god is the patron of craftsmen and architects
explanation: Ptah, the creator god of Memphis, is the patron of craftsmen, sculptors and architects.

question: Which god personifies magic
explanation: Heka, magic, travels in the bark of Re with Sia and Hu.

question: Which god personifies knowledge
explanation: Sia, knowledge, accompanies Re in his bark with Heka and Hu.

question: Which god personifies creative speech
explanation: Hu, creative speech, is part of the divine crew of the bark of Re.

question: Which desert region does the bark of Re cross in the fourth and fifth hours of the night
explanation: In the fourth and fifth hours, the bark crosses the desert of Sokar and must be hauled over the sand.

question: How many hours does the sun take to cross the sky during the day
explanation: The sun crosses the sky in twelve hours by day, then the underworld in twelve hours by night.

question: Which benevolent serpent coils around Re to protect him during the night
explanation: The serpent Mehen coils around Re to protect him at the deepest moment of the night.

question: Which goddess managed to obtain the secret name of Re
explanation: Isis shaped a serpent that bit Re, then only cured him in exchange for his secret name.

question: Which cobra goddess rears up, as the uraeus, on the brow of the king and the sun god
explanation: Wadjet, the cobra goddess, rears up as the uraeus on the brow of kings and gods.

question: Which demiurge rose from the Nun in the Heliopolitan cosmogony
explanation: Atum rose alone from the Nun and drew the first divine couple out of himself.

question: Who are the first children of Atum
explanation: Atum drew Shu and Tefnut out of himself, the first couple of Creation.

question: Which goddess swallows the sun in the evening and gives birth to it again in the morning
explanation: Every evening, Nut swallows the sun, which passes through her body during the night and is reborn in the morning.

question: Which god who died and rose again embodies the rebirth of vegetation
explanation: A god who died and rose again, Osiris also embodied the vegetation reborn after each flood.

question: Which moon god lights the night during the sun’s journey underground
explanation: While Re crosses the Duat, it is the moon of Thoth that lights the night.

question: What is the name of the cross that symbolises life
explanation: The ankh, the cross topped by a loop, means “life”; the rays of the Aten hold it out to the king.

question: Which god was the first to be mummified
explanation: Anubis anointed, purified and wrapped the body of Osiris: this was the first mummy.

question: In what animal form is the goddess Hathor shown
explanation: Hathor appears as a cow, as a woman with cow’s ears, or wearing horns around the sun disc.

question: In what animal form is the goddess Bastet shown
explanation: Bastet is the cat goddess of the home; originally a lioness, the cat is her calmed form.

question: In what animal form is the goddess Sekhmet shown
explanation: Sekhmet, “the powerful one”, is a lioness-headed goddess, the embodiment of divine anger.

question: Which city gave its name to the most widespread cosmogony in Egypt
explanation: The cosmogony of Heliopolis, whose creator is Atum, is the most widespread in Egypt.

question: What does the djet correspond to in a person
explanation: The djet is the body, which embalming was meant to preserve so that the ka and ba could return to it.

question: What does the ka correspond to in a person
explanation: The ka is the life force, born with the individual and fed after death by offerings.

question: Which rite gave the deceased back the use of their senses before burial
explanation: The Opening of the Mouth gave the deceased back the use of their senses, to speak, see and eat in the afterlife.

question: What is the symbol of the goddess Maat
explanation: Maat wears an ostrich feather, weighed against the heart of the deceased at the judgement.

question: What is the animal of the god Horus
explanation: Horus is the falcon god; his right eye was the sun, his left eye the moon.

question: Besides the ibis, what is the other animal of the god Thoth
explanation: Thoth is shown as an ibis-headed man or in the form of a baboon.

question: Which insect represents the god Khepri
explanation: Khepri is the scarab: the dung beetle pushing its ball evoked the sun pushed across the sky.

question: Which goddess personifies the order of the world, truth and justice
explanation: Maat is the order of the world established by the creator: truth, justice and balance.

question: Which creature devours the hearts of the dead judged unworthy
explanation: Amemet, “the Devourer”, eats the too-heavy hearts of the dead, who vanish for ever.

question: Which crocodile god is lord of waters and marshes
explanation: Sobek, the crocodile god, embodies the fearsome power of the Nile and the fertility it brings.

question: Which goddess has a bow and two crossed arrows as her emblem
explanation: Goddess of war and hunting, Neith has a bow and two crossed arrows as her emblem.

question: Which goddess is shown as a woman with a scorpion on her head
explanation: Selkis wears a scorpion on her head and protected against venomous stings and bites.

question: Which god is at the centre of the myth of the day cycle
explanation: The myth of the day cycle follows Re across the sky by day and through the underworld by night.

question: Of which god was every pharaoh considered the living incarnation
explanation: After his victory over Seth, Horus became the model for pharaohs, who reigned as a “living Horus”.

question: Which god plays the part of creator in the Memphite cosmogony
explanation: At Memphis, Ptah creates the world through the thought of his heart and the word of his tongue.

question: Which goddess is the wife of Horus of Edfu
explanation: Hathor is the wife of Horus of Edfu; their reunion was celebrated every year.

question: Which jackal-headed god is the patron of embalmers
explanation: Anubis mummified Osiris: during embalming, the chief priest wore his jackal mask.

question: What form does the sun god take at night, in the underworld
explanation: At night, in the underworld, Re takes the form of a ram-headed man.

question: Which part of the body of Osiris was swallowed by a fish
explanation: Isis found the whole body of Osiris except his phallus, swallowed by a Nile fish.

question: In the form of which bird did Atum appear on the Benben
explanation: Atum appeared on the Benben in the form of the Bennu, a bird the Greeks likened to the phoenix.

question: Which god separated the sky from the earth at Atum’s command
explanation: At Atum’s command, Shu lifted Nut above Geb, separating the sky from the earth.

question: How many gods make up the Ogdoad of Hermopolis
explanation: The Ogdoad of Hermopolis counts eight deities, forming four couples.

question: How many divine couples make up the Ogdoad of Hermopolis
explanation: Nun and Naunet, Heh and Hauhet, Kek and Kauket, Amun and Amaunet form the four couples of the Ogdoad.

question: With what heads were the goddesses of the Ogdoad shown
explanation: The goddesses of the Ogdoad had serpent heads, the gods frog heads.

question: With what heads were the gods of the Ogdoad shown
explanation: The gods of the Ogdoad had frog heads, an animal that seems to arise from the mud of the Nile.

question: What does the couple Nun and Naunet stand for in the Hermopolitan cosmogony
explanation: Nun and Naunet embody the primordial waters of chaos.

question: What does the couple Amun and Amaunet stand for in the Hermopolitan cosmogony
explanation: Amun and Amaunet embody what is hidden, invisible.

question: In which city was the great sanctuary of Ptah
explanation: Memphis was the city of Ptah; the name of his temple, Hut-ka-Ptah, gave us the word “Egypt”.

question: Which sacred animal was regarded as the living incarnation of Ptah
explanation: The Apis bull was the living incarnation of Ptah; it was buried in the Serapeum at Saqqara.

question: According to the Heliopolitan cosmogony, what were the first humans born from
explanation: Atum wept on finding Shu and Tefnut again, and his tears (remyt) became humans (remetch).

question: Which lioness goddess slaughtered the humans who rebelled against Re
explanation: The Eye of Re, in the form of Hathor, changed into the lioness Sekhmet to slaughter the rebellious humans.

question: Which ordeal decided the fate of the deceased in the afterlife
explanation: The heart of the deceased was weighed against the feather of Maat; if too heavy, it was devoured by Amemet.

question: Under what name was the Great Sphinx of Giza worshipped
explanation: The Great Sphinx of Giza was worshipped as Harmachis, “Horus in the horizon”, a form of the sun.

question: According to Memphite theology, how did Ptah create the world
choices: By shaping clay on his wheel
explanation: According to the Shabaka Stone, everything first exists as a thought in the heart of Ptah, then comes into being through his word.

question: Which god is the tongue of Ptah in Memphite theology
explanation: In Memphite theology, the heart of Ptah is Horus and his tongue is Thoth.

question: Which dwarf god with a grimacing face protected homes and births
explanation: Bes, a dwarf with a grimacing face, drove away demons and protected sleep and births.

question: What is the rearing cobra on the brow of the pharaohs called
explanation: The uraeus is the rearing cobra on the brow of the pharaohs, image of the goddess Wadjet.

question: What is the creature with a lion’s body and a human head called
explanation: The sphinx has a lion’s body and a human head; the one at Giza was worshipped as Harmachis.

question: What is the shining, immortal spirit of the justified dead called
explanation: After a favourable judgement, the ka and the ba come together to form the akh, the immortal spirit.

question: What does a person’s ren refer to
explanation: The ren is the name: as long as it was spoken, the deceased went on existing.

question: What does the name “Amun” mean
explanation: Amun, “the hidden one”, is an invisible creator, present everywhere but seen by no one.

question: What is the animal of the god Anubis
explanation: Jackals prowled around cemeteries: the Egyptians made this animal the guardian of tombs.

question: How many accomplices helped Seth shut Osiris in the chest
explanation: With seventy-two accomplices, Seth shut Osiris in a chest made to his size and threw it into the Nile.

question: Which god brought abundance by causing the yearly Nile flood
explanation: Hapi embodies the Nile flood, which every summer covered the fields with fertile silt.

question: Which god is the son of Amun and Mut
explanation: Khonsu, god of the moon, is the son of Amun and Mut, with whom he forms the Theban triad.

question: Which fertility god is shown wearing two tall plumes, his arm raised holding a flail
explanation: Min, god of fertility, wears two tall plumes and raises his right arm holding a flail.

question: Which goddess was the Upper Egyptian counterpart of the cobra goddess Wadjet
explanation: Nekhbet, the vulture goddess of the South, formed with Wadjet the “Two Ladies” who protected the king.

question: Whose daughter is Maat
explanation: Daughter of Re, Maat embodies the order of the world as the creator established it.

question: Which canopic jar did the goddess Selkis protect
explanation: Selkis watched over the canopic jar of the intestines, guarded by falcon-headed Qebehsenuef.

question: Which hippopotamus goddess protected pregnant women and childbirth
explanation: Tueris, a hippopotamus goddess with the belly of a pregnant woman, protected childbirth.

question: Which goddess of Sais watched over the canopic jars with Isis, Nephthys and Selkis
explanation: Neith watched over the canopic jars with Isis, Nephthys and Selkis, especially the one holding the stomach.

question: Which goddess is often shown nursing her son
explanation: Isis is often shown nursing her son Horus, the image of the protective mother.

question: Which god was held to be the inventor of hieroglyphs
explanation: Thoth was held to be the inventor of hieroglyphs, mathematics and the calendar.

question: Which god’s name means “the one above” or “the distant one”
explanation: The name of Horus evokes the falcon soaring high in the sky: “the one above”.

question: Which ram-headed god with horizontal horns shapes children on his potter’s wheel
explanation: Khnum, the “divine potter”, shaped children and their ka on his wheel.

question: What is the weighing of the heart also called
explanation: The weighing of the heart of the deceased against the feather of Maat is also called psychostasia.

question: Which goddess pins down Apophis during the night journey of Re
explanation: In the seventh hour of the night, Selkis pins down Apophis while the magic of Isis weakens him.

question: Under which pharaoh did the cult of the Aten supplant that of the other gods
explanation: The pharaoh Amenhotep IV made the Aten the only god of Egypt and took the name Akhenaten.

question: Where did Isis take refuge to hide the child Horus
explanation: Isis hid Horus in the marshes of Chemmis, in the heart of the Delta, to protect him from Seth.

question: In what animal form did Horus and Seth fight in the Nile
explanation: Changed into hippopotamuses, Horus and Seth dived into the Nile: the first to come up would lose.

question: Who tore out the eyes of Horus during their struggle for the throne
explanation: During their struggle for the throne, Seth tore out the eyes of Horus and buried them.

question: Which goddess restored the sight of Horus with gazelle milk
explanation: Hathor restored the sight of Horus by pouring gazelle milk on his eyes.

question: What is the healed Eye of Horus, which became a symbol of protection, called
explanation: The restored Eye of Horus, the udjat, became one of the most widespread amulets in Egypt.

question: By what trick did Horus win the stone boat race against Seth
answer: He used a wooden boat covered with plaster
choices: He used a wooden boat covered with plaster
He had Seth’s boat sunk with Sobek’s help
He stole Seth’s boat during the night
He asked Thoth to raise a storm
explanation: Horus built a boat of cedar wood covered with plaster; Seth’s, made of real stone, sank.

question: Who threatened the tribunal of the gods with sending his messengers if Horus was not crowned
explanation: From the world of the dead, Osiris threatened to send his demons if his son was not crowned.

question: For how many years did the tribunal of the gods hesitate between Horus and Seth
explanation: The tribunal of the gods, presided over by Re, hesitated for eighty years between Horus and Seth.

question: What role was Seth given after the crowning of Horus
answer: Driving back Apophis from the bark of Re
choices: Driving back Apophis from the bark of Re
Ruling the world of the dead
Becoming the messenger of the gods
Guarding the gates of the Duat
explanation: Seth joined Re in the sky: from the prow of the solar bark, he drives back Apophis.

question: How many scorpions escorted Isis as she crossed the Delta with Horus
explanation: Seven scorpions escorted Isis: Tefen, Befen, Mestet, Mestetef, Petet, Tjetet and Matet.

question: On which magical stela was the spell against scorpion venom copied
explanation: The spells of Isis and Thoth were copied onto magical stelae such as the Metternich Stela.

question: Why can Apophis never be destroyed
choices: Because he lives in the Nun, out of reach
Because Re makes him whole again
explanation: Apophis existed before Creation and was never created: he therefore cannot be destroyed.

question: Which ritual did priests recite to help Re defeat Apophis
explanation: The priests made a wax figurine of Apophis, then trampled, pierced and burned it.

question: Nefertem is the god of which flower
explanation: Nefertem is the god of the blue lotus, the flower that opens at dawn, and of perfumes.

question: Who are the parents of Nefertem in the Memphite triad
explanation: At Memphis, Nefertem forms a triad with his parents, Ptah and Sekhmet.

question: Which crown does the god Sokar wear
explanation: Sokar, falcon god of the necropolis of Memphis, wears the atef crown.

question: What is the name of Sokar’s sacred bark, carried in procession at his festival
choices: The bark of millions of years
explanation: At the festival of Sokar, his sacred bark, the Henu, was carried around the walls of Memphis.

question: What does the name of the god Wepwawet mean
explanation: Wepwawet cleared the way for the king in processions, and for the dead to the afterlife.

question: Where was the main cult centre of Wepwawet
explanation: Wepwawet was worshipped at Asyut, which the Greeks called Lycopolis, “the city of the wolf”.

question: Which god plays the part of creator in the Theban cosmogony
explanation: At Thebes, Amun “the hidden one” formed himself at the beginning; all the gods are his manifestations.

question: In the form of which serpent did Amun appear at the dawn of the world
explanation: According to late texts, Amun appeared in the form of the serpent Kematef, “he who has completed his time”.

question: Which serpent, begotten by Kematef, created the Ogdoad in the Theban cosmogony
explanation: Kematef begot Irta, “he who made the earth”, who in turn created the Ogdoad.

question: Which temple became the largest religious complex ever built in Egypt
explanation: Enlarged over nearly two thousand years, the temple of Amun at Karnak is the largest in Egypt.

question: Where was the great temple of Isis, still active until the 6th century AD
explanation: The temple of Isis at Philae stayed open until the 6th century, long after the other cults had ended.

question: Where was the main sanctuary of Khnum
explanation: Khnum was worshipped on the island of Elephantine, where he formed a triad with Satet and Anuket.

question: Where was the great cult centre of Bastet, whose festival Herodotus described
explanation: Herodotus describes the festival of Bastet at Bubastis, which drew hundreds of thousands of pilgrims.

question: What are the two great cult centres of the god Sobek
explanation: Sobek shared a double temple at Kom Ombo and reigned over the Faiyum, where sacred crocodiles were kept.

question: Which pharaoh particularly favoured the cult of Sobek in the Faiyum
explanation: The Middle Kingdom pharaoh Amenemhat III particularly favoured the cult of Sobek in the Faiyum.

question: Which city, centre of the cult of Neith, was the capital of the 26th Dynasty
explanation: Neith was the great goddess of Sais, capital of Egypt under the 26th Dynasty.

question: Where was the sanctuary of Nekhbet, the vulture goddess
explanation: The sanctuary of Nekhbet was at Nekheb, present-day El Kab, in Upper Egypt.

question: Where was the cult centre of Wadjet, the cobra goddess
explanation: The cult centre of Wadjet, Buto, lay in the Nile Delta.

question: Which pharaoh bore the name of the god Seth
explanation: Long respected for his strength, Seth gave his name to the pharaohs Seti I and Seti II.

question: With which Greek god was Thoth identified
explanation: The Greeks identified Thoth with Hermes, messenger of the gods and patron of letters.

question: Which god is the heart of Ptah, the seat of thought, in Memphite theology
explanation: In Memphite theology, Horus is the heart of Ptah, the seat of thought, and Thoth his tongue.

question: On which monument, given to the British Museum in 1805, is the Memphite theology carved
explanation: The Shabaka Stone was given to the British Museum in 1805, when no one could read hieroglyphs.

question: Which composite deity results from the merging of Ptah, Sokar and Osiris
explanation: Ptah merged with Sokar and Osiris to form Ptah-Sokar-Osiris, god of creation, death and rebirth.

question: How did the gods stop Sekhmet’s slaughter
choices: By locking her in the Duat
By asking Thoth to put her to sleep
By offering her the throne of Egypt
explanation: Re had beer dyed with red ochre poured out; Sekhmet drank it, got drunk and forgot her anger.

question: On the back of which heavenly animal did Re leave the earth
explanation: Weary of ruling, Re climbed onto the back of Nut, changed into a heavenly cow, and left the earth.

question: What did Isis use to shape the serpent that bit Re
explanation: Isis mixed with earth the saliva that the ageing Re let drip, and shaped it into a serpent.

question: What does the name of the goddess Nephthys mean
explanation: Nephthys wears on her head the hieroglyphs of her name: a house topped by a basket.

question: Who placed themselves under the protection of the goddess Sekhmet
explanation: Held responsible for epidemics, Sekhmet could also cure them: physicians placed themselves under her protection.

question: Which divine triad does Khnum form at Elephantine
explanation: At Elephantine, Khnum formed a triad with the goddesses Satet and Anuket.

question: With which god was Wepwawet sometimes confused, because of their shared funerary role
explanation: Wepwawet opened the way of the dead to the afterlife, a role that brought him close to Anubis.

question: What does the name of the god Atum mean
explanation: His name means both “the Complete One” and “the One who does not yet exist”: before Creation, Atum held within himself everything that was to be.

question: Into which animal will Atum turn at the end of time
explanation: One text announces that at the end of time, Atum will destroy everything he has created and become a serpent again, alone in the waters of the Nun.

question: Which crown does Atum most often wear
explanation: Atum is the king of the universe: he most often wears the double crown of Upper and Lower Egypt.

question: What does the Egyptian verb kheper, from which Khepri takes his name, mean
explanation: Khepri’s name comes from the verb kheper, “to come into being, to transform”: he is the sun reborn every morning.

question: Where was a scarab amulet placed on mummies
explanation: A symbol of rebirth, the scarab was placed over the heart of mummies to ensure the deceased a new life.

question: What did the Greeks call Horus the Elder
explanation: The Greeks called this falcon sky god Haroeris; he must not be confused with Horus, the son of Isis and Osiris.

question: With which god did Horus the Elder share the double temple of Kom Ombo
explanation: At Kom Ombo, Horus the Elder shared a double temple with the crocodile god Sobek, each of them holding one half.

question: What are the eyes of Horus the Elder
explanation: Horus the Elder is a falcon god of the sky: his eyes are the sun and the moon.

question: Which gods travel with Heka in the bark of Re
explanation: Heka travels in the bark of Re with Sia, knowledge, and Hu, creative speech: the forces with which the sun creates and protects the world.

question: At Esna, which gods were Heka’s parents
explanation: At Esna, Heka was worshipped as a divine child, son of Khnum and Neith, shown with a finger raised to his mouth.

question: What is Seshat the goddess of
explanation: Seshat, companion or daughter of Thoth, is the goddess of writing, reckoning and records.

question: Which animal’s skin does Seshat wear
explanation: Seshat is shown as a woman dressed in a leopard skin, wearing a seven-pointed star and holding the scribe’s reed pen.

question: On what did Seshat write the names of the pharaohs
answer: The leaves of a sacred tree
choices: The leaves of a sacred tree
explanation: Seshat kept the record of the pharaohs’ regnal years, writing their names on the leaves of the sacred tree of Heliopolis.

question: During which ritual did Seshat help the king fix the site of a temple
explanation: During the ritual of “stretching the cord”, Seshat helped the king pull taut the rope that fixed the exact site of the future sanctuary.

question: What is Montu the god of
explanation: Montu is the god of war: pharaohs called themselves “mighty as Montu” in battle.

question: What does Mentuhotep, the name of several kings of the 11th Dynasty, mean
explanation: Several kings of the 11th Dynasty bore the name Mentuhotep, “Montu is satisfied”.

question: Which animal embodied Montu’s strength
explanation: Montu is sometimes shown as a bull-headed man, the animal that embodied his strength.

question: Satet and Anuket are the goddesses of which region
explanation: Satet and Anuket watched over the First Cataract of the Nile, on the southern border of Egypt, with Khnum.

question: What was thrown into the river during the flood to celebrate Anuket
explanation: During the flood, Anuket was celebrated by throwing coins, gold and jewellery into the river.

question: What does the name of the goddess Satet mean
explanation: Satet, “she who pours”, was charged with pouring the cool waters of the flood over Egypt.

question: What does the name of the goddess Mut mean
explanation: Mut, “the mother”, is the wife of Amun and the mother of Khonsu, with whom she forms the Theban triad.

question: Which bird, used to write her name, is associated with Mut
explanation: Mut sometimes wears a vulture headdress: the bird that writes her name is a symbol of motherhood.

question: Which pharaoh had hundreds of statues of Sekhmet placed in the temple of Mut
explanation: Mut could be fearsome like Sekhmet: Amenhotep III had hundreds of statues of the lioness goddess placed in her temple to soothe her anger.

question: Which title did Amun-Re bear in the New Kingdom
explanation: In the New Kingdom, Amun-Re, “king of the gods”, became the supreme god of Egypt, creator of the world and father of the pharaoh.

question: When was Amun joined with Re, as kings from Thebes took power
explanation: When kings from Thebes took power in the Middle Kingdom, their god Amun was joined with Re to give him national standing.

question: Where did the Distant Goddess flee, changed into a lioness
choices: To the marshes of the Delta
explanation: Wounded that another had taken her place, the goddess fled, changed into a lioness, into the deserts of Nubia, south of Egypt.

question: In what form did Thoth approach the Distant Goddess
explanation: To approach the lioness without frightening her, Thoth took the form of a small baboon, then soothed her with words and fables.

question: In the fable told by Thoth, which animal saves the lion
explanation: A lion spares a mouse which later saves him by gnawing through the ropes of a net: even the weakest have their place in the order of the world.

question: In what form did Re place his Eye on his brow so she would never leave again
explanation: So that the goddess would never leave again, Re placed her on his brow in the form of a rearing cobra, the uraeus, guardian of his crown.

question: Which festival celebrated the return of the Distant Goddess each year, notably at Dendera
explanation: The goddess’s return coincided with the flood: it was celebrated every year with a Festival of Drunkenness, notably at Dendera in honour of Hathor.

question: In the reign of which king is the story of the Famine Stela set
explanation: Carved in the Ptolemaic period, the stela tells of a famine in the reign of Djoser, the builder of the first pyramid.

question: For how many years did the Nile flood fail, according to the Famine Stela
explanation: For seven years the flood had not come: grain was scarce and the temples themselves were closed.

question: Which wise adviser revealed the secret of the flood to the king
explanation: Imhotep, the priest and architect of the Step Pyramid at Saqqara, consulted the sacred books and revealed the secret of the flood to the king.

question: According to Imhotep, where did the Nile gush from
explanation: Imhotep revealed that the Nile gushed out of two caverns beneath the island of Elephantine, whose lord was Khnum.

question: According to historians, why did the priests of Khnum have the Famine Stela carved
explanation: Competing with the priests of Isis at Philae, the priests of Khnum attributed their rights over the region to Djoser to give them the authority of age: a “pious forgery”.

question: What does the word “demiurge” refer to
explanation: In each cosmogony, the god of the city plays the part of the demiurge, the creator of the universe (from the Greek dēmiourgos, “craftsman”).

question: Which was the most widespread of the Egyptian cosmogonies
explanation: The most widespread is that of Heliopolis, whose creator is the solar demiurge Atum, often identified with Re.
